findings: Both frozen K modules were read in full, together with current K task/README, exact J hstarts sources and REGISTRY/REPORT/review, the original manuscript/compiler and entire causal finite-approximation source. Current production rounded, beta, Euler, Rosser and lower projection definitions were read directly.

The actual ALL/ANY coefficient is defined on the complete divisor universe of the target-deleted rough prime product. Positive Mobius coefficients use ALL membership of their full label cell in the raw retained support; negative coefficients use ANY intersection. The same complete history is tested, and no prefix-closure property is imposed on the rounded output.

ANY rounding can produce negative coefficients outside the raw retained support. K does not apply the old retained-support mass theorem to these cells. It identifies the entire compiler universe with the divisors of the exact rough prime product, then uses the actual coefficient absolute bound at every divisor in that full universe.

Rough primes retain the actual cap, primality, p not dividing N, closed lower endpoint w and strict upper endpoint z. Sorting is Nodup and preserves the finite prime product. The exact reciprocal-totient divisor sum is the product of 1+1/(p-1). Modulus one and the empty rough interval are included; no signed density is substituted for absolute mass.

Evenness deletes the prime2. On each odd prime the plus factor is bounded by the inverse Goldbach factor. The actual foundational inverse-interval theorem has one Krough>1 before every finite odd-prime subset and all real 2<=w<=z, with closed lower and strict upper endpoints. Its theorem and proof were inspected; no assumed dimension-one bound or completeness of the enumeration cap is inserted.

The power envelope uses z<=D^r and monotonicity of the logarithm, giving (r/epsilon^2)*(1+Krough/(epsilon^2*log D)). The constant and bound are independent of retained policy and mesh, including outward cells. Intermediate start cutoffs are covered by one common top r.

The actual small Euler normalization retains every target-prime deletion and its strict endpoint. Its supplier identifies the strict cutoff with the inclusive Mertens product at ceil(w)-1, uses the actual singular-series correction and positive twin-prime constant, and yields V<=B*singularSeries(N)/log w for positive even N, w>=4 and a cap covering w. K derives all these gates.

The actual small Rosser density error is C*(exp(-1/epsilon)+exp(sqrt K-1/epsilon)*(epsilon*log D)^(-1/3)). The same lower/upper weights and target-deleted carrier have an existing density sandwich with constants before epsilon and a threshold before N/cap. Its source fundamental-lemma statement and the uniform progression-density dimension-one adapter were inspected at their actual WSL files.

The full beta loss is exactly V*E times the reciprocal-totient absolute mass of the rounded rough coefficient. The finite lower-attachment proof uses beta-minus for nonnegative c and beta-plus for negative c. Its absolute-mass loss bound requires neither nonnegativity of beta-minus nor nonnegativity of the signed main.

Euler normalization and rough mass each cost epsilon^-2. K correctly uses the epsilon^-4 scalar absorption. It chooses epsilon below both1/8 and the arbitrary earlier positive epsilonMax so the exponential floor is already below eta; only then does it choose D large enough to absorb the logarithmic remainder and make w>=4. It never claims a fixed-epsilon error tends to zero.

The real-D reserve has epsilon and D0 before D,N,cap,z,tau and retainEven. Assumptions remain C>0,r>0,eta>0,epsilonMax>0; positive even N; cap covering w; and w<=z<=D^r. K is a real auxiliary constant. Arbitrary tau is legitimate for this mass bound because every constructed coefficient has absolute value at most one; meaningful approximation by a positive mesh is a separate obligation.

The grouped specialization retains D=N^(249/448), cap=ceil(N^h), and both actual cutoffs N^a,N^h. J supplies the common small-beta gates from0<epsilon<1/8, and the top rough power is exactly D^(h/nu)=N^h. No root is silently reduced to1/2 and no physical support bound for arbitrary rough policies is inferred.

The real-D request is eta*nu/4. Since log D=nu*log N, each start receives eta/4 on the singularSeries/log N scale. The literal3+1 combination is therefore at most eta on that scale. One epsilon and one natural threshold serve both policies and the shared mesh.

rawMain=roundingMain-betaLoss is definitional for the same J expression. The grouped beta bound gives a lower comparison after subtracting eta*singularSeries/log N. Multiplication uses the actual nonnegative pi(N), not an assumed sign of either raw main. The resulting theorem has the literal original3*currentChenUpsilon1+currentChenUpsilon2 right-hand side.

The retained sharp errors are exactly the original signed total-pi errors of the same rounded physical rho used in the pointwise minorant. J's centre proof sums that same polynomial over excluded prime receivers first, yielding one-sided cost at most4*omega(N); its existing delta*singularNormalization payment is retained. Neither the signed polynomial nor the centre error is replaced by an absolute modulus-incidence estimate.

The final main still contains the complete full-policy raw density minus the exact Euler-weighted ALL/ANY roundingLoss. No causal endpoint, gate-strip smallness, hstarts bound, physical coefficient-class licence or PP estimate is a premise or conclusion of the new export.

The uniform beta/count statement alone allows arbitrary finite policies after N because their unestimated sharp and rounding terms remain. It does not license a moving policy for the final asymptotic PP argument. The original fixed-policy approximation order and its actual causal histories remain mandatory.

The original grouped endpoint still includes3*savedL1+savedL2+ordinaryStartChange-removedH248+weightedSixIntegrals+slantedRestoration. J's ordinary root density is only a baseline. Neither it nor the new beta payment supplies the original causal gains or the final PNT-normalized supplier.
